title: Plain task data
description: What fromTasks and mount({ tasks, links }) read. Extra fields on a task or a link are allowed and are not read. validate() adds the checks a schema cannot state: ids that repeat, a parent or link that names a task that is not there, and a progress key (actualFinish, resume, and remaining unless options.unstartedRemaining is on) with no actualStart, or remaining with progress.

dataDate.description: The day the update is as of. Work that has not started cannot start before it. A date alone is 00:00 of that day.

mustFinishBy.description: The date the project must finish by. Float is measured against the earlier of it and the computed finish, so a date the plan cannot meet shows as negative float. A date alone is the end of that day.

options.description: The schedule options (decision 0018). A member left out keeps its default; an unknown member is refused.

startedLateStart.description: The late start a started, unfinished task shows: p6, the late start of its remaining work; project, its actual start.

unstartedRemaining.description: on: a task that has not started and has a remaining duration is scheduled with that length; off: remaining is ignored until the task starts.

calendars.description: The working calendars. A task's calendar names one by key; the first is every other task's. Without them, the one Monday to Friday calendar, 08:00 to 17:00 with an hour at noon.

durationUnit.description: What every duration, remaining and lag counts. days (default): a day is the working day of the calendar that measures the value; an hour is 60 working minutes. A part of a minute is rounded to the nearest.

lagCalendar.description: The calendar a lag day is counted on: successor (default), predecessor, 24h, or the key of a calendar.

calendar.description: The key of a calendar in calendars.
Give workDays with hoursPerDay, or week, not both. A calendar's day, the length a days duration counts, is hoursPerDay, or the average worked day of its week.

key.description: Your own text id for the calendar, unique among the calendars; a task's calendar and lagCalendar name it.

workDays.description: The worked weekdays, 1 for Monday to 7. Each is worked from 08:00 for hoursPerDay hours.

hoursPerDay.description: Hours worked on each of workDays.

week.description: Seven lists of [from, to] minutes of the day, Monday first, in order; one day at least has a period.

exceptions.description: Days that differ from the week, one entry for each day.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. A day before the schedule's first Monday is left out and named in leftOut.

working.description: true: an extra working day, with the hours of the calendar's first worked weekday. false: a holiday.

id.description: A task id: text or a number, unique among the tasks.

name.description: The text shown for the task.

duration.description: In the data's durationUnit: working days of the task's calendar, by default.

calendar.description: The key of one of the data's calendars; the first when left out.

parent.description: The id of the summary task this one sits under.

color.description: The bar's color as #rrggbb, with no alpha. Any other text is left out and named in leftOut. The name on the bar stays readable for the tested palette only.

label.description: The text the bar shows in place of the name. The task list keeps the name. Any other kind of value is left out and named in leftOut.

key.description: The host's own text id for the task, such as a database id. It is kept through edits and saves and the app never reads it. Send a number as text.

snet.description: Start no earlier than. Read in place of start when given. A date alone is the first working minute of that day on the task's calendar.

snlt.description: Start no later than. A date alone is the first working minute of that day on the task's calendar.

fnet.description: Finish no earlier than. A date alone is the end of the last working minute of that day on the task's calendar.

fnlt.description: Finish no later than. A date alone is the end of the last working minute of that day on the task's calendar.

mso.description: Must start on. One pin per task: mso or mfo, not both. A date alone is the first working minute of that day on the task's calendar.

mfo.description: Must finish on. A date alone is the end of the last working minute of that day on the task's calendar.

constraint.description: The one date limit of the task, { type, date }, or null for none. It is the limit its type names, wins over start (which may then be left out), and is not given with snet, snlt, fnet, fnlt, mso or mfo. so (start on) is snet and snlt on one date, and fo (finish on) is fnet and fnlt on one date: neither moves the bar, and float can go negative. A date alone is read as the member of its kind reads it.

alap.description: true schedules the task as late as possible.

milestone.description: On a task with no duration: start sits at the start of a working period, finish at the end of one.

actualStart.description: When the task actually started. A date alone is the first working minute of that day.

actualFinish.description: When the task actually finished; needs actualStart. A date alone is the end of the last working minute of that day.

remaining.description: Work left, in the data's durationUnit; needs actualStart, and is not given with progress.

resume.description: When paused work picks up again; needs actualStart.

type.description: Defaults to FS, finish to start.

lag.description: In the data's durationUnit (working days of the lagCalendar, by default); negative for lead.

key.description: The host's own text id for the link. It is kept through edits and saves and the app never reads it.
